drug_class: Estrogen combined with a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat moderate to severe hot flashes caused by menopause. It helps reduce how often and how intense those sudden feelings of heat and sweating are. It is only for women who still have a uterus and have not had a hysterectomy.
how_it_works: The estrogen part of this pill helps relieve menopausal symptoms like hot flashes by replacing some of the estrogen your body is no longer making. The bazedoxifene part acts like a protector for your uterus, reducing the risk of uterine problems that estrogen alone can sometimes cause. Together, they work as a team so you get relief without needing a separate progestin.
common_side_effects: Some women notice muscle spasms or cramps, nausea, diarrhea, upset stomach, throat pain, dizziness, or neck pain. You might also have some hot flashes or sweating, especially in the first few weeks of taking it.
warnings: This medicine carries important risks. It may increase the chance of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack, especially if you smoke or are older. It should not be used to prevent heart disease or dementia. Women with a history of breast cancer, blood clots, liver problems, or unexplained vaginal bleeding should not take this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you have unusual vaginal bleeding, chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Your doctor will recommend using the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed.
